newsitem.title: USA: Penn Traffic bonds rally on new CEO rumors.
newsitem.headline: Penn Traffic bonds rally on new CEO rumors.

text.p: Penn Traffic Co bonds jumped six points as market rumors swirled that Penn was close to hiring a chief executive officer, traders said.
"The bonds have been all over the place and now have settled in a bit," one high-yield trader said.
Penn Traffic 9.625 percent paper traded at a high of 54 bid before settling in at a 47-1/2 bid, 47-3/4 offer, still 1-1/4 points higher at the close, players said.
The rumor also suggested current chairman Gary Hirsch, who has been acting CEO for the past five months would be departing, traders said.
Chief Financial Officer Eugene Sunderhaft would neither confirm nor deny the hiring rumor.
Sunderhaft added that it is his understanding that Hirsch would remain at Penn.
Hirsch was not immediately available for comment.

"We are currently in an active search. The search process has been going on and we've said quite consistently that when we have finanlized an arrangement we will make an announcement - that has not happened yet," Sunderhaft said.
Meanwhile, other Penn Traffic issues were quoted higher by about a point, traders said.
The 11.50 percent bonds were quoted at an 87 bid, while the company's 8.625 percent paper were quoted between 83-1/2 bid and 84 bid, traders added.

Penn Traffic has been recently plagued by a series of negative same-store sales reports pompting credit rating agency, Standard & Poor's, to revise the company's outlook to negative from stable in January.
Penn Traffic expects to report its full fourth quarter financial results in mid-March.
